entry: Marginal sea of the northwestern [[Pacific Ocean]], bounded by the [[Kamchatka Peninsula]] and [[Kuril Islands]] on the east, [[Hokkaido]] on the south, [[Sakhalin]] on the west, and the eastern coast of [[Siberia]] on the west and north. It covers 1,583,000 square kilometres (611,000 sq mi), with a mean depth of 859 metres (2,818 ft) and a maximum depth of 3,372 metres (11,063 ft). It is the coldest sea in East Asia and the southernmost sea in the Northern Hemisphere that freezes over seasonally. Sea ice forms in the northwest and expels salt into deeper layers; the resulting heavy water flows east, carrying oxygen and nutrients that support abundant sea life. Warming has driven fish populations north: the salmon catch on the northern Japanese coast has fallen 70% in 15 years. South Sakhalin and the Kurils were administered by Japan until 1945, and Japan still claims the southern Kurils.

Marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific, the heaviest member of the [[Mustelidae|weasel family]]. Adults weigh 14–45 kg (30–100 lb). Lacking a blubber layer, it relies on the densest fur of any animal for insulation. Sea otters dive to the sea floor for [[Sea urchin|sea urchins]], mollusks and crustaceans, and they are among the few mammals to use tools, using rocks to open shells. In most of their range they are a keystone species, since their predation keeps sea urchins from destroying [[Kelp]] forests. Hunted for their fur between 1741 and 1911, they fell to 1,000–2,000 individuals. Protection and reintroductions have restored them to about two-thirds of their former range, but the species remains [[Endangered species|endangered]], as populations in the Aleutian Islands, California and Russia have declined.

Common name for two groups of venomous elapid snakes: the true sea snakes (subfamily Hydrophiinae), about 62 species that spend their lives in the ocean, and the sea kraits (genus *Laticauda*), about 8 semi-aquatic species that return to land to breed. True sea snakes give birth to live young in the water, while sea kraits lay eggs on land. Their streamlined bodies have paddle-like tails, and they absorb oxygen through the skin during long dives. Their neurotoxic venoms are among the most potent of any reptile, but they are generally docile and rarely bite unless provoked, such as when caught in fishing nets. About 10% of species are assessed as at elevated risk of extinction and lack international protection under treaties such as CITES.

Marine [[Reptile|reptile]] of the superfamily Chelonioidea, with seven living species. Five of the seven are listed as threatened with extinction on the IUCN Red List. The leatherback is the largest, reaching 1.4 to more than 1.8 m (4.6 to 5.9 ft) and weighing 300–640 kg (661 to 1,411 lb); the Kemp's ridley is the smallest, at 60 cm (2 ft). Unlike many other [[Turtle|turtles]], sea turtles cannot pull their heads and limbs into their shells, but their streamlined bodies let them swim swiftly. Adult males have long tails with the cloacal opening near the tip. Females return to natal beaches to excavate nests and lay clutches of leathery eggs. Sea turtles face fisheries bycatch, habitat loss and marine debris.

Spiny, globular [[Echinoderm|echinoderm]] forming the class Echinoidea. Approximately 950 species live on the seabed in every ocean, from the intertidal zone to the deep sea. Typically 3 to 10 cm (1 to 4 in) across, they move on hundreds of tube feet and have a rigid test covered in movable spines. Most feed on algae, though they also eat slow-moving animals such as sponges and crinoids. Their predators include sharks, [[Sea otter|sea otters]] and humans. Unchecked by predators, urchins can create barrens devoid of large algae. The fossil record dates from the Ordovician period, some 450 million years ago. Because their embryos are transparent and easy to observe, sea urchins have been a [[Model organism|model organism]] in developmental biology since the 19th century.

Bottom of an [[Ocean|ocean]], also called the seafloor, sea floor or ocean floor. Its structure is governed by [[Plate tectonics|plate tectonics]]. Most of the ocean is very deep, and its floor there is the [[Abyssal plain|abyssal plain]]. [[Mid-ocean ridge|Mid-ocean ridges]] form along the centers of major ocean basins through seafloor spreading. The seabed slopes up from the abyssal plain through the continental rise and slope to the [[Continental shelf|continental shelf]]. Most of it is covered by marine sediments, classified by origin as terrigenous, biogenous, hydrogenous or cosmogenous, and by size from clay and silt to sand and boulders. Ships use acoustic technology to map its depths, but only 27.3 percent had been mapped at high resolution as of mid-2025. Human activity affects it through plastic pollution, mining and dredging.

[[Bird|Bird]] adapted to life in the marine environment, including [[Albatross|albatrosses]], [[Penguin|penguins]] and [[Gull|gulls]]. Seabirds show convergent evolution, as similar environmental problems and feeding niches have produced similar adaptations. The first seabirds evolved in the [[Cretaceous]] period, and modern families emerged in the [[Paleogene]]. They generally live longer, breed later and have fewer young than other birds, but invest heavily in them. Most species nest in colonies ranging from a few dozen birds to millions. Many make long annual migrations, some circumnavigating the Earth. Supraorbital salt glands excrete the salt taken in with seawater. Longline fishing bycatch is the main cause of mortality for over 100 species, and oil spills, climate change and offshore development also threaten them. Conservation includes wildlife refuges and changes to fishing methods.

American champion [[Thoroughbred]] racehorse. Small and slow to start, he won only a quarter of his first 40 races, but became the top money-winning racehorse up to the 1940s and a symbol of hope during the [[Great Depression]]. He beat the 1937 Triple Crown winner War Admiral by four lengths in a two-horse special at Pimlico and was voted American Horse of the Year for 1938. The film *Seabiscuit* (2003) was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture.

Sea life regarded as food by humans, chiefly [[Fish|fish]] and shellfish. Shellfish include bivalve mollusks such as clams, oysters and mussels; [[Cephalopod|cephalopods]] such as octopus and squid; [[Crustacean|crustaceans]] such as shrimp, crabs and lobster; and echinoderms such as [[Sea urchin|sea urchins]]. Seafood is an important source of animal protein, especially in coastal areas, and the Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend at least 8 ounces a week. Global production exceeds 200 million tonnes a year, and aquaculture now surpasses wild capture fisheries. Seafood has been eaten since the Paleolithic: *Homo sapiens* at Pinnacle Point in South Africa harvested marine life as early as 165,000 years ago. Mercury in some predatory species has prompted consumption advisories.

Genus (*Hippocampus*) of small marine bony fishes related to pipefish. Seahorses swim upright, with a horse-like head, a curled prehensile tail and bony plates in place of scales. They range from 1.5 to 35 cm (0.6 to 13.8 in) long and are poor swimmers, propelled by a dorsal fin and steered with tiny pectoral fins. They are ambush predators that suck up small [[Crustacean|crustaceans]]. Females deposit eggs into a brood pouch on the male, where he fertilizes and carries them until the young are born. Most live in shallow tropical and temperate waters, often among [[Coral reef|coral reefs]], [[Mangrove|mangrove]] roots and seagrass beds, where they camouflage themselves. They are threatened by coastal development and by harvesting for the [[Aquarium|aquarium]] trade and traditional Asian medicine. All species are listed under CITES Appendix II.

Underwater mountain that rises at least 1,000 m above the seafloor without reaching the surface. Seamounts are typically formed from extinct [[Volcano|volcanoes]] and usually rise 100–4,000 m (330–13,120 ft). If a summit reaches the surface, wave erosion can flatten it; once it subsides, it becomes a flat-topped guyot, or tablemount. More than 14,500 seamounts have been identified, most in the North Pacific. They attract [[Plankton|plankton]], corals, fish and marine mammals, making them among the most common marine ecosystems, and many support fisheries. Bottom trawling causes 95% of their ecological damage, and stocks such as orange roughy have declined. Flank collapses can cause landslides with the potential to generate [[Tsunami|tsunamis]].

American rapper, record producer and entrepreneur. Combs is credited with discovering or developing [[The Notorious B.I.G.]], [[Mary J. Blige]] and [[Usher (musician)|Usher]], and he founded Bad Boy Records in 1993. His debut album *No Way Out* (1997) topped the Billboard 200. He founded the clothing company Sean John in 1998 and co-founded the television network Revolt in 2013. In 2025 he was convicted of transportation to engage in prostitution and acquitted of racketeering and sex trafficking charges, and he was sentenced to 50 months in prison.

Scottish actor and producer who was the first actor to portray [[James Bond]] in films. He starred in seven Bond films between 1962 and 1983, beginning with *Dr. No*, and worked with directors such as [[Alfred Hitchcock]] and John Huston, including on *Marnie* and *The Man Who Would Be King*. For *The Untouchables* (1987) he won the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for Best Supporting Actor, becoming the first Scottish actor to win a major Oscar. He also won a BAFTA for *The Name of the Rose*. He was knighted in 2000 for services to drama. He publicly supported Scottish independence and the Scottish National Party, and in later life he lived mainly in the Bahamas.

American conservative television host and political commentator. Hannity has hosted a self-titled program on [[Fox News]] since 2009, and he hosts *The Sean Hannity Show*, a nationally syndicated talk radio program. He co-hosted *Hannity & Colmes* on Fox from 1996 until 2009. He was inducted into the National Radio Hall of Fame in 2017 and has written four *New York Times* best-selling books. A strong supporter of [[Donald Trump]], he has drawn criticism for his commentary on the 2020 election.

American entrepreneur and philanthropist who co-founded the file-sharing service Napster with Shawn Fanning. He was the first president of [[Facebook]] and co-founded Plaxo and Brigade, an online platform for civic engagement. As a teenager he was sentenced to community service after hacking into a company network. He founded the Parker Foundation, which focuses on life sciences, global public health and civic engagement. In May 2025 Forbes estimated his net worth at US$3.0 billion.

American actor and filmmaker. Penn has won three [[Academy Awards|Academy Awards]]: Best Actor for *Mystic River* (2003) and *Milk* (2008), and Best Supporting Actor for *One Battle After Another* (2025). His other films include *Fast Times at Ridgemont High*, *Dead Man Walking* and *Into the Wild*, which he directed in 2007. He did humanitarian work after [[Hurricane Katrina]] and the 2010 Haiti earthquake, and he has supported Ukrainian president [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] during the Russian-Ukrainian war.

Software system that returns links to [[World Wide Web|web]] pages and other information in response to a user's query. Search engines use automated crawlers to index content, then rank results by factors such as keyword relevance and link authority. Early tools included Archie, created in 1990 by Alan Emtage at McGill University in [[Montreal]] to index the file names on public FTP sites. [[Google Search|Google Search]] became the dominant engine in the 2000s. As of May 2025, Google held about 89–90% of worldwide search share, and that month marked the first time in over a decade that its share fell below 90%. Because of this dominance, search engine optimization has focused largely on Google.

Scientific effort to detect signals or other evidence of intelligent life beyond Earth, usually shortened to SETI. Methods include monitoring electromagnetic radiation with [[Radio telescope|radio telescopes]], searching for optical signals and investigating possible artifacts. Modern searches began in the early 20th century after the advent of radio. Projects include Project Ozma, SETI@home and Breakthrough Listen, a $100 million, 10-year effort announced in 2015 by [[Stephen Hawking]] and Yuri Milner. Despite decades of searching, no confirmed evidence of alien intelligence has been found. Critics call SETI speculative and unfalsifiable, while supporters see it as a step toward addressing the [[Fermi paradox]].

American department store chain and online retailer, founded as a mail-order business by Richard Warren Sears and Alvah Curtis Roebuck. It opened its first retail stores in 1925 and was the largest retailer in the United States through the 1980s, until it was surpassed by [[Walmart]] in 1989. A 2005 merger with Kmart created Sears Holdings, which filed for Chapter 11 [[Bankruptcy|bankruptcy]] in October 2018. Its successor, Transformco, has focused on selling off remaining real estate. From 2,705 stores at its peak in 2011, only five were still open in the U.S. as of December 2025.

Most populous city in the U.S. state of [[Washington (state)|Washington]], on an [[Isthmus|isthmus]] between Puget Sound and Lake Washington. Its population was 784,777 in 2025, and the metropolitan area exceeds 4.15 million. Native peoples, including the Duwamish, had lived in the area for at least 4,000 years before European settlement. Settlers led by Arthur A. Denny arrived in 1851, and the settlement was named for Chief Seattle. Logging and shipbuilding were early industries, and after World War II [[Boeing]] made the city a center of aircraft manufacturing. From the 1980s, technology firms including [[Microsoft]] and [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] expanded the economy. Seattle was also home to grunge, with [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]] and [[Pearl Jam]] among its bands, and the coffee chain [[Starbucks]] began there in 1971.

Macroscopic, multicellular marine [[Algae|algae]], comprising thousands of species. The term covers the [[Red algae|red]], [[Brown algae|brown]] and [[Green algae|green]] groups, which do not share a single common multicellular ancestor. Kelp and other seaweeds provide nursery habitat for fisheries, and planktonic algae produce at least 50% of Earth's oxygen. Mechanical dredging of [[Kelp]] destroys the resource and the fisheries it supports, and a wasting disease in predators of purple urchins led to urchin surges that destroyed large kelp forests off California. Seaweed farming, long practiced in [[East Asia]], supplies food, carrageenan and fertilizer. Cultivation is also studied as a way to absorb [[Carbon dioxide|carbon dioxide]], and the IPCC recommends further research into it.

Portuguese statesman and diplomat who was the leading minister of King Joseph I from 1750 to 1777. He secured his preeminence through his management of the [[1755 Lisbon earthquake|1755 Lisbon earthquake]], organizing relief and supervising the rebuilding of the capital. After the Távora affair of 1759 he suppressed the [[Jesuits|Society of Jesus]] and oversaw the execution of leading members of the aristocratic opposition. A strong advocate of absolutism influenced by the Enlightenment, he centralized government and introduced mercantilist reforms, including royal monopolies and chartered trading companies. His policies also promoted the Atlantic slave trade to Brazil, while banning the import of Black slaves into mainland Portugal. He fell from power in 1777 and was exiled, and his legacy remains highly controversial.

German former racing driver who competed in [[Formula One|Formula One]] from 2007 to 2022. He won four consecutive World Drivers' Championships with Red Bull from 2010 to 2013 and 53 Grands Prix overall, including nine in a row in 2013. At Ferrari he was the closest challenger to [[Lewis Hamilton]] and finished runner-up in 2017 and 2018. He retired after the 2022 season. Since 2023 he has been co-owner of the Germany SailGP Team, and he is an environmental and climate activist.

Conflict fought between 1899 and 1902 between the [[British Empire]] and the Boer republics, the South African Republic and the Orange Free State, in [[South Africa]]. It was triggered by the discovery of gold in the Transvaal and a dispute over voting rights for British immigrants (Uitlanders). Boer forces initially won victories and besieged British garrisons, but British armies under Lord Roberts and Lord Kitchener occupied both republics and their capitals, [[Pretoria]] and [[Bloemfontein]], by 1900. Boer guerrillas fought on for two years, and Britain responded with scorched-earth tactics and concentration camps, where tens of thousands of civilians died. The Treaty of Vereeniging in May 1902 ended the war, and in 1910 the former republics joined the Union of South Africa within the British Empire.

Medieval Bulgarian state in the [[Balkans|Balkans]] that existed from 1185 to 1396. It succeeded the [[First Bulgarian Empire]], and until 1256 it was the dominant power in the Balkans, defeating the [[Byzantine Empire]] in several major battles. Tsar Kaloyan defeated the Latin Empire at Adrianople in 1205, and his nephew [[Ivan Asen II]] extended Bulgaria from the Adriatic to the Black Sea. The empire declined in the late 13th century under invasions by Mongols, Byzantines, Hungarians and Serbs, and it was divided into three parts before the Ottoman invasion. Its capital, Tarnovo, was considered a "New Constantinople" and became the cultural hub of the Eastern Orthodox world in the 14th century.
